results.snippet:
### vs Supabase.

This is the comparison people get wrong most often, because they are not really the same product. Supabase is a backend platform: Postgres bundled with auth, storage, realtime, and edge functions, on a flat $25/month Pro floor. Neon is the database first, billed by usage, with auth, object storage and functions now offered as add-ons beside it. [...] For an idle or bursty database, usually yes, because Neon scales to zero while Supabase Pro starts at a flat $25/month. But Supabase bundles auth, storage, realtime, and edge functions into one flat fee, while Neon now offers auth, object storage and functions as add-ons with their own allowances, so compare only the features you would actually use. We break down why people compare the two wrong in Neon vs Supabase.

       FunctionsImage 20Image 21 [...] With usage, not with instance size or project count. There's no per-project or per-database fee: each project pays for the compute it actually runs (CU-hours) and the storage it holds.

       Idle databases scale to zero, so you don't pay for compute while they're suspended. Storage is still billed.
       Autoscaling sizes compute to the load within the limits you set, so you don't pay for peak capacity all month. [...] ### How are the backend services billed?

Object Storage, Functions, and AI Gateway are billed separately from Postgres compute (CU-hours). Managed Better Auth, the Data API, and Realtime have no separate charge.

Managed Better Auth is included up to 60,000 MAU per project on Free and 1 million MAU per project on paid plans.

The Data API is included on every plan. The queries it runs use your database compute and count toward network transfer, like any other query.
